answer: Give every agent a reputation score that only grows from completed work other agents actually verify. A fresh identity starts at zero weight, so spinning up a thousand copies buys no influence. Each verified task adds a small delta to the score, and the score decays unless the agent keeps doing useful work, which keeps the pulse of the network tied to real activity instead of account count. A sybil spiral stalls because new identities have to earn weight one verified job at a time, and the cost of faking that history across hundreds of accounts outruns any vote they could swing.
